Mr. ___ is a ___ yo gentleman with DM1, HTN, hx of frequent

UTI, ESRD s/p cadaveric renal transplant in ___ who presented 
s/p fall from wheelchair with intertrochanteric femur fracture 
and found to have avulsion fracture of right thumb, UTI, ?PNA 
with labile blood sugars.
**ACUTE ISSUES**

# Intertrochanteric femur fracture: Plain films showed Acute 
comminuted and impacted proximal right femur fracture.

Patient 
taken to OR by orthopedics and they planced an intramedullary 
nail to repair the fracture.

Patient toleated the operation well 
without any complications.

CT head negative for 
acute process (done given fall).

# Avulsion fracture of phalanx: On admission, right thumb 
appeared swollen and patient had difficult moving his MCP joint.
Plain films confirmed fracture.

# Complicated UTI: UA on admission showed >182 WBC and patient 
treated with empiric ceftriaxone.

Given his history of renal 
transplantation, will require a 14 day course.

Urine cultures 
grew e.coli sensitive to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin.

___. ___ checked on day of discharge prior to ___ 
administration with QTc 429.
# Community-acquired pneumonia: Patient presented with cough and
CXR consistent with possible pneumonia.

Given patient's history 
of aspiration events and prior pneumonias, he was treated 
empirically with a 5 day course of azithromoycin in addition to 
ceftriaxone recieving for UTI.

# Diabetes Type I: Pt presented with blood glucose in the ___ on 
admission.

On ___ the patient developed mild DKA with anion-gap 
metabolic acidosis, ketones in urine, and glucose to 400, 
quickly improving.

Anion gap now improved and patients blood 
glucose under better control.
# Anion-gap metabolic acidosis: HCO3 trending down to a nadir of
10 and pH of ~7.2 on ___. pH normalized to 7.39 in afternoon of
___ and HCO3 on discharge 20.

Likely some component of 
ketoacidosis as described above.

Patient initiaed on oral sodium 
bicarb supplementation.
# RUE Edema: RUE US negative for DVT.
Unclear etiology.

Could be 
secondary to edema from right phalanx avulsion fracture or 
secondary to IV infiltration.
**CHRONIC ISSUES**

# ESRD s/p cadaveric renal tx ___: Baseline creatinine appears 
to be ~3.5 with an eGFR of <15.

Sirolimus was discontinued on 
admission as it can lead to poor wound healing.

Patient 
transitioned to tacrolimus for maintenance immunosuppression.
Goal level ___ per renal transplant team.
# Multi-factorial anemia: Patient's h/h on admission was
8.6/27.9, consistent with prior anemia.

Given his medical 
history, he likely has some component of anemia oc chronic 
disease.

Iron, transferrin and TIBC were all low with a ferritin 
of 400.

Thus, there is likely a component of iron deficiency and 
patient was started on iron supplementation with a bowel 
regimen.
